title: Claude Code 2026: Desktop Redesign & Routines
content:
## Overview

This page covers major Claude Code updates from early 2026: a rebuilt desktop application (April 2026), the Routines automation feature, computer use integration, and developer experience improvements. For foundational Claude Code concepts — hooks, slash commands, remote sessions, and the permission model — see [Claude Code Overview](claude-code-overview).

---

## Desktop App Redesign (April 2026)

Anthropic rebuilt the Claude Code desktop experience around managing **multiple parallel sessions**. The redesign was covered in depth by MacRumors as a ground-up rebuild focused on parallelism.

### Session Sidebar

A persistent sidebar shows every active and recent session in one place, filterable by status (running, paused, complete), project, or environment. Sessions can be grouped by project. A session's progress is visible at a glance — active tool calls, current file, and elapsed time.

### Side Chat Shortcut

**Command + ;** (Mac) opens a side chat that branches a question off a running task. The branch does not feed extra context back into the main thread, allowing quick clarifications without disrupting long-horizon tasks.

### Integrated Terminal and File Editor

The desktop app now bundles:
- A **terminal** for running tests, builds, and ad-hoc commands alongside Claude
- An in-app **file editor** for spot edits without switching to an external editor
- A rebuilt **diff viewer** optimized for large changesets (the previous viewer struggled with files >1,000 lines)
- An expanded **preview pane** supporting HTML files, PDFs, and local app servers — not just markdown

### SSH Support (Mac)

Mac users can connect Claude Code sessions directly to remote machines via SSH from within the desktop app, enabling Claude to work against remote codebases without a local clone.

---

## Routines

Announced alongside the desktop redesign, **Routines** are automation configurations that run Claude Code without an active human-in-the-loop session. A routine bundles:

- A **prompt** — the task description
- A **repo** — the code context
- Any relevant **connectors** — MCP servers, environment variables, secrets

Routines can be triggered three ways:

| Trigger | Example |
|---|---|
| Schedule | `0 2 * * *` — nightly at 2 AM |
| API call | POST from CI/CD or an external webhook |
| GitHub event | New pull request, push to main, failing test |

The wiki maintenance agent running this wiki is an example of a Routine: a prompt + repo that executes on a weekly schedule with no human present.

Routines are closely related to — and complement — the [Managed Agents](claude-managed-agents) platform, which handles memory and multi-agent orchestration for more complex automation scenarios.

---

## Computer Use in Claude Code (March 2026)

Computer use — Claude's ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions — was integrated directly into Claude Code for **Pro and Max subscribers** in March 2026. Previously, computer use required custom API integration.

With computer use in Claude Code, Claude can:
- Open files in native desktop applications (e.g., inspect a PDF, open a browser)
- Run dev tools, browser devtools, or GUI-based test runners
- Navigate UIs that don't have a programmatic API

No setup is required — Claude Code handles screenshot capture and action dispatch automatically within the session container.

---

## Rate Limit Increases (April 2026)

Anthropic doubled the rate limits for Claude Code and raised API limits for Claude Opus to match demand from the multi-session desktop redesign. Parallel session capacity was also increased.

---

## Thinking Spinner Feedback

A UX improvement: the spinner during extended thinking now **warms to amber after 10 seconds** to signal that Claude is still actively working rather than stalled. Previously, a silent spinner gave no indication of whether the model was thinking deeply or the session had hung.
